lastText: The Night EndsThe ReleaseNew Ending Discovered · 1 / 15A FOREIGN GENTLEMAN LEAVES A HOUSE AT PURFLEETYou stand in the hall at Carfax and tell each of them they are free. Some weep. Some do not understand. A man in a nightshirt asks if he may have a bird. Then you open the doors and walk down the drive. In the morning the hall is empty and the house is cold. A woman in the house at Purfleet puts a hand to her forehead, as if something had been taken from it, and sits down. You go home alone, down a long road and a quiet one, and for the first time in centuries nobody is waiting at the end of it. In the tellings that outlast the newspapers, the foreign nobleman is remembered as a gentleman who asked for nothing but a house and a little company. A housemaid says he was the politest man she ever served. A solicitor's widow says he kept her husband's letters in a drawer after he died.
